a 13-year old boy who was bitten by a tick at age 3.5 developed a post-encephalitic syndrome that was initially misdiagnosed as Landau-Kleffer Syndrome.
the patient presented with a history of developmental delays, regression, seizures, and abnormal EEG findings.

TBE can present with LKS symptoms, and that LKS can occur as a sequelae to TBE.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the differential diagnosis of LKS and TBE in an autistic child should be considered when a child presents with regression in developmental and language milestones, and seizures, as well as abnormal EEG findings, as these are common features of LKS and post-encephalitic syndrome (PES).
LKS should be considered as a differential diagnosis in patients with a history of tick bites and a clinical presentation that is consistent with the condition.
